clues: This city sits atop a chain of ridges in Mizoram, in the far north-east of India. It is the largest town of its small hill state.
Most rain here falls from April to October, with the most in May and the late summer months. The rest of the year stays much drier and cooler.
From 1898 to 1947, this city was the seat of rule for the British in these hills. That is a span of near five decades at the top of these hills.
The Red School still stands in the heart of town. So does Raj Bhavan, a grand old hall from British days.
This city is home to the Assembly House of its state. All the main work of the state's rule is done from here.
